newsitem.title: USA: Dollar rises on news U.S. trade gap shrank in March.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rises on news U.S. trade gap shrank in March.

text.p: The dollar rose against most currencies on Wednesday after the Commerce Department reported that the U.S. trade deficit shrank a surprisingly large 19.3 percent in March, dealers said.

Also, U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin gave the dollar a boost in late trade by assuring markets the administration's policy for a strong dollar will remain unchanged and that a strong dollar is "good" for the economy because it leads to lower interest rates and lower inflation.
But the dollar's gains were limited as nerves were still frayed by Tuesday's steep slide in the dollar after Federal Reserve officials elected not to raise U.S. interest rates.

"The market is very confused. People are very unsure about the direction and there have been such big swings that it's hard to establish any type of view," said James Powers, a vice-president in foreign exchange sales and advisory at Westdeutsche Landesbank in New York.
The dollar rose to 1.6943 marks from 1.6770 at Tuesday's close and to 114.35 yen from 112.63.
The overall U.S. trade gap shrank to $8.5 billion in March, well below market forecasts for a deficit in excess of $10.0 billion.

A surprise 4.1 percent jump in U.S. exports prompted economists to upwardly revise their final estimates for first-quarter U.S. economic growth to roughly 6.0 percent from the current 5.6 percent preliminary estimate issued weeks ago by the Commerce Department.
"It smells like 6 percent," said Commerce Undersecretary Everett Ehrlich. The boost to the first quarter's growth measure supported the dollar, dealers said.
However, the headline trade figure masked an 8.3 percent rise in the United States' bilateral trade gap with Japan.
The dollar got some support from Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Koebnick, who said he had little objection to the dollar trading at 1.70 marks -- slightly above its current trading level.
However, U.S. markets offered the dollar little support as the Dow Jones industrials index fell almost 13 points and the 30-year benchmark Treasury lost two-thirds of a point.

In Asia, Japanese officials tried to repair damage done on Tuesday after members of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party called for a rise in the official discount rate, which currently sits at a record low of 0.5 percent.

On Wednesday, Takahiro Kawase, director of the Bank of Japan's policy planning department, told reporters that the central bank has no plans for an immediate rise in interest rates. Separately, Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a parliamentary committee that Japanese politicians should refrain from commenting on interest rates.
Mitsuzuka also said recent worries over an excessive weakening of the yen have completely disappeared.

In other trading, the dollar rose to 1.4080 Swiss francs from 1.3865 at the open after officials at the Swiss central bank added liquidity to the market and said there was no fundamental reason for the currency's recent rise.
The dollar rose to Canadian $1.3675 from C$1.3670 and the British pound fell to $1.6447 from $1.6565.
